questions.question: What histologic finding most reliably distinguishes immune-mediated necrotising myopathy from polymyositis or dermatomyositis?
Which laboratory result most effectively indicates that an elevated creatine kinase reflects muscular injury rather than liver damage?

In patients who develop proximal limb-girdle weakness several weeks after initiating a GLP-1 receptor agonist yet lack detectable anti-HMGCR or anti-SRP antibodies how should empiric treatment typically be started?

What findings drive clinicians toward diagnosing drug-induced immune mediated necrotising myopathy instead of statin toxicity related rhabdomyolysis,
inclusion body myositis or viral myocarditis?

When proximal weakness evolves roughly four months after a single dose of semaglutide—with serial creatine kinase rising modestly initially then exceeding four thousand IU/L—what does this time course argue favor an autoimmune process rather than an acute toxic injury?

Describe the cellular cascade—from antibody binding through complement activation—to precipitate macrophage-mediated ‘myofiber phagocytosis’ characteristic of seronegative immune mediated necrotising myopathy.
Why did pro-B-type natriuretic peptide rise markedly while left ventricular ejection fraction remained preserved during this illness episode?

After symptom resolution treated empirically with steroids plus IVIG and permanent discontinuation of semaglutide is routine maintenance immunosuppression justified,and why does durable improvement often occur rapidly?
